skill.name: browser-testing-with-screenshots
skill.description: Automates Chrome browser testing workflows with visual verification, element selection, page inspection, and screenshot-based evidence collection.
skill.summary: Run browser-based UI checks with screenshots, element picking, and page inspection.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate browser testing documentation, but it relies on third-party browser control commands with access to active Chrome sessions. Confirmed risks include remote browser automation, screenshot capture, cookie listing, page-context JavaScript execution, and extraction of page content. I found no prompt injection text and no evidence of screenshot upload, but the local capture and session access risks remain significant.

remediation.issue: Browser sessions and cookies can be exposed.
remediation.suggestion: Default to fresh test profiles, remove cookie listing from quick reference unless required, and warn users not to use personal sessions.

remediation.issue: Screenshots can capture sensitive page data.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear guidance for test accounts, redaction, retention, and deletion of screenshot artifacts.

remediation.issue: browser-eval.js runs code inside the page context.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to avoid production pages and review JavaScript snippets before execution.

remediation.issue: The skill depends on external agent-tools from GitHub.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed version, document verification steps, and explain exactly which commands users will run.

content.value_statement: Visual UI bugs are hard to confirm from logs alone. This skill guides browser-driven checks with screenshots, element picking, and page inspection.
actual_capabilities: Launches Chrome through browser-start.js with remote debugging enabled.
Navigates web pages with browser-nav.js for local application testing.
Captures viewport screenshots with browser-screenshot.js for visual evidence.
Uses browser-pick.js to choose page elements for later automation.
Runs browser-eval.js to inspect or change page state in the browser context.
Extracts readable page content and cookie information through browser tools.
limitations: Requires the external agent-tools package to be installed and available in PATH.
Examples assume a local development web application and Chrome access.
Screenshots and cookies can expose sensitive data if used on personal sessions.
Element selection may require human interaction and can be slower than headless tests.

use_cases.title: Verify Local UI Changes
use_cases.description: Check a development page after code changes and capture screenshots for review.

use_cases.title: Collect Visual Test Evidence
use_cases.description: Document login, dashboard, and profile flows with screenshots from a real browser.

use_cases.title: Debug Dynamic Element Selection
use_cases.description: Use interactive picking when selectors are unstable or generated by the application.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Page Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Confirm that one local page loads correctly.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to open my local app, navigate to the dashboard, and capture one screenshot for visual verification.

prompt_templates.title: Form Flow Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Test a login or signup flow with visible evidence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to test the login form, pick the fields and submit button, and capture screenshots before and after submission.

prompt_templates.title: Dynamic UI Inspection
prompt_templates.scenario: Inspect a page that loads content after user interaction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to navigate through the dynamic page, wait for loaded content, inspect key elements, and capture screenshot evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Page Evidence Run
prompt_templates.scenario: Collect visual evidence across several application pages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to test login, dashboard, and profile pages, organize the screenshots, and summarize any visual or interaction issues found.

output_examples.input: Test the dashboard page after a local frontend change.
output_examples.output: The dashboard loaded, the navigation menu was visible, and a screenshot was saved for review.

output_examples.input: Verify that the login form can be filled and submitted.
output_examples.output: The username and password fields were selected, the form was submitted, and the final page state was captured.

output_examples.input: Collect evidence for login, dashboard, and profile pages.
output: Dashboard page screenshot captured after navigation.
Profile page screenshot captured and named for review.

best_practices: Use test accounts and fresh browser profiles when screenshots or cookies may contain sensitive data.
Wait for page load or a specific element before capturing screenshots.
Keep screenshot evidence in a dedicated test-results directory with clear page names.
anti_patterns: Do not run browser-eval.js on production pages unless the action is reviewed first.
Do not capture screenshots from personal browser sessions or accounts with sensitive data.
Do not rely only on hardcoded selectors when the UI uses dynamic element identifiers.

faq.question: Does this skill install browser tools by itself?
faq.answer: No. It requires agent-tools to be installed separately and available in the system PATH.

faq.question: Can it test applications running on localhost?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples focus on local development servers and browser-based UI checks.

faq.question: Does it support visual verification?
faq.answer: Yes. It captures browser screenshots so users can review the visible page state.

faq.question: Can it interact with dynamic page elements?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses interactive element picking when static selectors are hard to maintain.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with real user sessions?
faq.answer: Use caution. Screenshots, cookies, and page content can expose private data from active sessions.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for full test frameworks?
faq.answer: No. It is best for visual checks, debugging, and evidence collection alongside other tests.
